title: EEG: eyes open and closed
summary: Alpha waves appear over the back of the head when the eyes close.
description: Five channels of a 64-channel EEG: Fp1 (on the forehead), Cz (on top of the head) and O1, Oz and O2 (over the occipital cortex, at the back). The first part was recorded with the eyes open, the second (a separate run of the same session) with the eyes closed. With the eyes closed, rhythmic alpha waves of about 10 a second appear at the back of the head; opening the eyes blocks them. The large slow waves in Fp1 with the eyes open are blinks: the eye is electrically charged, so moving it changes the potential near the forehead.
look_for: The alpha waves in O1, Oz and O2 with the eyes closed, and their absence with the eyes open
The frequency of the alpha waves: measure the time of several waves with the calipers

subject.notes: One of the 109 volunteers of the dataset (age and sex not given).
